title: DR1 names the part of the notification above the heading on nearly every journey page; the frontend shows a caption on only the five address picker pages.

finding.frontend: Only five of the 40 captured screens show anything above the page heading: the address pickers, which print "Consignment addresses" in a `govuk-caption-l` from `src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.njk:7`. That is the only caption in the whole frontend. On every other journey page the slot above the heading holds either nothing or the journey strip — a blue "Draft" tag beside the notification reference, `src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:64-69` — so a user part-way through a notification is never told on the page itself which section of the task list they are working in.
finding.prototype: 36 of DR1's 42 screens print a caption immediately above the heading, and on 32 of those it names the part of the notification. Read from the rendered DOM, the captions are "About the consignment" on eleven screens (origin of the import, what are you importing and its results, reason for import with its error state and its four revealed states, consignment details, animal identification), "Consignment parties" on six (roles and addresses in its three states, consignment address select, CPH number, permanent address), "Documents" on all seven upload states, "Add a new transporter" on the three add-a-transporter pages, "Transport and arrival" on two (transporter, arrival details), "Movement" on two (transit countries, empty and selected) and "Commodity details" on one (additional animal details). The remaining four are the dashboard's own "Dashboard", which names the page rather than a part of a notification and is covered by the dashboard title finding. `app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:39-40` shows the pattern: a caption paragraph then the heading. The six DR1 screens with nothing above the heading are the declaration, the submitted page, the two review states, the contact address page and the notification hub.
finding.difference: Add a caption above the heading on each journey page naming the section it belongs to, taking the wording from DR1 page by page. Two of DR1's captions do not agree with DR1's own task-list section headings — it captions the additional animal details page "Commodity details" where its task list says "2. Description of the goods", and the transit countries page "Movement" where its task list says "3. Transport and arrival" — and those two need a designer's word before they are copied across, because the frontend's own task list happens to use "Commodity details" and "Movement" as its section names. The other captions can be copied as they stand. This is independent of any work on what the task-list sections are called.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a caption above the heading on a frontend journey page other than the five address pickers.
finding.verification: Re-counted from the rendered DOM on both sides — the page model is unusable here, since it reports `caption: null` on every prototype screen because it looks for `govuk-caption-*` where DR1 renders `app-*__caption` — and opened the fe-origin, dr1-origin-of-the-import, fe-declaration and dr1-declaration full-page shots. The frontend side holds exactly: `govuk-caption-l` appears in 5 of the 40 DOMs, all five address pickers, all reading "Consignment addresses", and party-picker.njk:7 is the one place it is written. I checked the other caption-shaped classes in the frontend DOMs in case one of them was a page caption — `app-commodity-total__caption` (fe-hub and fe-hub-exit-details-blocked) and the `govuk-table__caption` set are card and table labels, not page captions — and fe-origin.html has nothing at all between the grid column and its `<h1>`. The journey strip is as described and is not a caption. Ran the falsifier: no frontend journey page outside the five pickers carries one, so it does not fire. The two caption-versus-task-list mismatches in `difference` both check out against dr1-notification-hub's own section headings, which are "2. Description of the goods" and "3. Transport and arrival" where the captions say "Commodity details" and "Movement", and against fe-hub, whose sections are "2. Commodity details" and "3. Movement". Two prototype-side counts were wrong; see the correction.
finding.correction:
The finding stands and the frontend side is exact. The prototype side was wrong twice, both times by trusting a file-level match on `__caption`. First, "37 of DR1's 42 screens print a caption immediately above the heading" was 36. dr1-notification-hub matches `__caption` but has no page caption: its `

Overview

` is at line 246 and its two `app-notification-hub-card__caption` elements — "Total number of animals in this consignment" and "Total number of packages in this consignment" — are card labels below it, at lines 258 and 268. So the hub belongs in the without list, which is six screens rather than five. Second, the enumeration of which screens carry which caption omitted three things: arrival details, which carries "Transport and arrival" alongside the transporter page; the reason-for-import error state, which carries "About the consignment" alongside the base page and the four revealed ones; and the four dashboard captures, which carry "Dashboard". The dashboard four are a caption above a heading but they name the page, not a part of a notification, so they are stated separately here and the work on them sits with the dashboard title finding rather than this one. Both slots rewritten with the counts re-derived screen by screen; the change asked for is unaffected.

relatedTo.why: The same caption element. That finding owns the dashboard's "Dashboard" caption, which this one deliberately leaves out because it names a page rather than a part of a notification.
